GENUINE. 0.24/1k against 1.0, with no second_regex to rescue it. Reading the mudborn lines confirms the deference is carried by the address form 'dry-one' (19.14/1k, passes) and by hedged clause-stacking the authored regex does not describe. A spec defect rather than a prose defect, but real either way.

THE METRIC IS MEASURING THE WRONG FEATURE. dw/sent 0.23, d<=6w 10.5pp, dSTTR 0.036 — statistically identical. To the ear they are nothing alike: 'Friend, this one was taught the depth and this one was taught the season' against 'Do not draw in the street. Do not argue with a writ.' Both terse; one servile (third-person self-reference 24.05/1k, 'friend' 42.40/1k), one imperative ('citizen' 9.45/1k). §B's separation rule offers only two length measures and one diversity measure and no measure of MOOD, while the corpus already holds the discriminating evidence in the address and grammar_tic blocks.

score.band_label: Excellent writing, imperfectly joined to the world — the prose axis is the strongest in this project and a tenth of it cannot be heard
score.note: Min over six axes: prose-as-written 8, signposting/AR-2 8, honesty 7, CONSUMPTION 6, topic graph 5, voice instrument 5. A reader who takes 5.0 as 'mediocre' will be wrong about the round in both directions. biggest_gap.what: Forty infos are written for `a` values no NPC record carries, including all 23 `magister` lines — an entire RI-DLG06 §B archetype (row 2, the Telvanni-analogue), whose register voice-metrics.mjs measures and whose bands speakers.json sets. infoFor() matches info.a === npc.actor exactly, so none of it reaches a player. A further 90 infos are gated to an (actor, town) pair no such actor stands in. Total: 133 of 1,280 infos (10.4%) that no character in a 5,400-strong player space can hear from any of 347 speakers, against a reported 3. The nine near-misses are the worst: notary-sedda-vell exists and is tagged actor 'archivist'; harbourmistress-tesh exists and is tagged 'clerk'; eleven scribes exist and are tagged 'clerk'. A topic `magister-varo-dren` answers 'I am he' and Varo Dren is not in the roster at all.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This project's own rule is that from the player's chair a model with no consumer and a missing model are the same thing. Ten percent of the best writing in the build does not exist, and it is the ten percent the voice system is scored on. The reason it survived a full round is that the two instruments that should have caught it cannot: build-graph.mjs's unreachable-INFO lint implements RI-DLG01 §A's first-match-wins rule while converse.js infoFor() scores specificity instead (0 ties in 75,948 resolutions, so authored order decides nothing), and shadow-audit.mjs audits only the three records that lint nominated.

remedy.action: (1) Add an NPC record for the House Dres magister the corpus already names, or an actor_aliases table mapping magister->dres-factor, notary->archivist, scribe/harbourmistress->clerk; nine of the forty are people who already exist under a different actor tag. (2) Add a CHECK, not a constructor assert (RULES 14): every info.a must appear in game/data/npcs/**, and every (a, cell) pair must have at least one speaker; exit non-zero. (3) Promote tools/dialogue/critic-reach.mjs or an equivalent to the gate in place of the superset lint, because the superset lint tests a rule the engine does not implement. (4) DECIDE FIRST, because everything above depends on it: either implement first-match-wins in infoFor() as RI-DLG01 §A requires, or amend RI-DLG01 §A to specify the scoring rule and rewrite the §D step-4 lint to match.

corpus_extended.what: §A mandates first-match-wins and §D step 4's lint is written for it; the shipped reader scores specificity instead and the item has no language for that case. The item should either hold the line or adopt the scoring rule explicitly and republish step 4. It should also say whether a topic advertised by an NPC's own record — a fourth entry point the item's step-2 orphan definition does not contemplate alongside root and journal-added — counts as an orphan. This verdict rules that it does, on the item's plain words.

§B's pairwise separation rule has no mood axis, and a fifth shape of failure is missing from the item entirely: THE ARCHETYPE WITH NO SPEAKER. An archetype can meet every band, pass every tic and separate from all five others while no NPC in the world carries its actor tag. §B should require that each archetype's line corpus be reachable from at least one shipped speaker before any of its bands are scored.

A fifth shape of the failure: THE INSTRUMENT THAT DOES NOT READ ITS OWN SPEC. voice-metrics.mjs is named by speakers.json as its checker and ignores five of the fields that file declares for it, turning a passing archetype into a reported failure. RI-MTH07 asks whether the world reads the model; it does not ask whether the CHECKER reads the model, and a checker with unread spec fields produces false failures that a builder will then try to fix in the prose.
